review.translation: [But mist|0] [would rise|1] [from|2] [the earth|3] [and water|4] [the whole|5,6] [surface of|7] [the ground|8].

analysis.evidence: אֵד is the subject of יַעֲלֶה מִן הָאָרֶץ, “would rise from the earth,” and of וְהִשְׁקָה, “would water.” Both verbs describe moisture rising from the earth and watering the whole surface of the ground. The verse leaves open whether it rose as mist or as liquid water.
analysis.morphology: וְ־ conjunction + masculine singular absolute noun

analysis.evidence: יַעֲלֶה agrees with אֵד, “mist,” as its subject. The phrase מִן הָאָרֶץ, “from the earth,” identifies the starting point of its upward movement.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, third person masculine singular

analysis.evidence: In יַעֲלֶה מִן הָאָרֶץ, “would rise from the earth,” מִן introduces הָאָרֶץ as the place from which the mist rises.
analysis.morphology: Independent preposition without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: מִן הָאָרֶץ identifies the ground as the source from which the אֵד rises. The following clause names the surface it waters, כָּל־פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “the whole surface of the soil.”
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ + common noun, singular absolute.

draft.change: Add a Hiphil sense for watering the ground alongside the existing sense of giving someone drink.
draft.definition: To supply the ground with water.
draft.evidence: In Gen.2.6 the rising אֵד supplies moisture to the whole surface of the ground.

analysis.evidence: The אֵד rises from the earth and waters it. The direct object marker אֶת introduces כָּל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “the whole surface of the ground,” identifying what receives the moisture.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וְ followed by the Hiphil perfect, third person masculine singular. The weqatal continues יַעֲלֶה and shares its subject, אֵד.

analysis.evidence: אֶת introduces כָּל־פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “the whole surface of the ground,” as the direct object of וְהִשְׁקָה, “watered.”
analysis.morphology: Unsuffixed direct-object particle, with no prefix.

analysis.evidence: In וְהִשְׁקָה אֶת כָּל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, כָּל specifies the extent of what was watered: the whole surface of the ground.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular noun in the construct state.

analysis.evidence: In וְהִשְׁקָה אֶת כָּל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “and watered the whole surface of the ground,” פְּנֵי stands in construct with הָאֲדָמָה and denotes the surface that receives the water.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, common gender, plural construct of פָּנִים, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In כָּל פְּנֵי הָאֲדָמָה, “the whole surface of the ground,” פְּנֵי means “surface of,” and הָאֲדָמָה identifies the ground whose surface receives the water.
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, with the prefixed definite article הָ.
analysis.sense: the ground underfoot; the face of the earth
